correctness.rationale: For every 0<K<1, work in the canonical real lift. Orientation preservation and exact rotation 1/2 permit consecutively ordered period-two points. Subtracting the two lifted equations gives 2d=K cos(m) cos(d); adding gives detuning. This two-equation representation is reversible and continuous. Eliminating the midpoint reduces the width to one-variable maximization; the boundary endpoints give zero, and its unique critical point solves the strictly increasing Q(d)=K^2. A separate symmetric midpoint maximization proves R=4pi W/K^2 is strictly decreasing because d increases with K and sinc(2d) decreases, with the maximizer always interior. The analytic implicit expansion d=A-A^3/2+13A^5/24+O(A^7) and maximization at m=pi/4+K^2/24+O(K^4) yield the stated coefficients. Exact symbolic power-series coefficient checks and numerically independent root/variational and direct second-iterate calculations corroborate; finite computations are not used to prove the universal claims.

originality.rationale: The fully inspected Schilder-Peckham working paper supplies precisely the same sine-map family and numerical tongue computations, including the 1/2 tongue, but not this global exact root equation or a strict normalized-width theorem. The 2023 perturbative tongue calculation gives a leading small-coupling approximation rather than the finite-coupling monotonicity. Davie 1996 is genuinely close by object and title: accessible abstract describes a different large-denominator asymptotic, and the full article could not be accessed, leaving a stated priority risk rather than establishing noncoverage. No corresponding result was found in actual semantic published-finding corpus searches or own archival/current claims, but absence of a hit is not proof of uniqueness. The complete evidence weighs against implication by inspected antecedents; priority remains unconfirmed.

value.rationale: Tongue width is the canonical frequency-locking measure for a rational resonance. Its exact dependence on the coupling strength throughout the entire invertible domain, together with a strict normalized monotonicity and sharp universal quadratic envelope, gives a structural finite-amplitude statement not contained in leading perturbation theory. The exact one-root characterization is computationally practical for any K and provides a sharp boundary for detuning versus forcing. Not a single parameter substitution or arbitrary restricted case: 1:2 is the simplest nontrivial resonance with no first-order width and is routinely used as the benchmark for subharmonic entrainment. No claim of a broad q theorem or experimental interpretation beyond this natural invariant.
